key_insight: Rubric-guided large language models can closely match expert grading of Linux/bash exam answers, but accuracy drops as command complexity increases.
engineering_relevance: A taxonomy-based triage can help automate grading for simpler command tasks while routing harder, higher-level questions to human instructors.
method: 1200 real student responses graded by 3 expert instructors
Compared 4 frontier LLMs: GPT, Claude Opus, Gemini, and GLM
Tested minimal vs rubric-enhanced prompts across a 4-level cognitive taxonomy
evidence_signal: Gemini 3.0 Pro with rubric prompting achieved the best agreement with experts (ICC(3,1)=0.888, MAE=0.10, bias=-0.014).
watch_item: Performance declines at higher taxonomy levels, so AI grading should be limited to questions where equivalent solutions and structural nuance are well captured.
paper_title: Automated grading of Linux/bash examinations using large language models: a four-level cognitive taxonomy approach
